title: Job 36
paragraphs: ¹ Elihu went on and said: ² "Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you that there is more to say on God's behalf. ³ I will draw my knowledge from afar, and ascribe righteousness to my Maker. ⁴ For truly my words are not false; one who is perfect in knowledge stands before you.

⁶ He does not keep the wicked alive, but gives justice to the afflicted. ⁷ He never takes his eyes off the righteous; he sets them on thrones with kings and exalts them forever. ⁸ But if they are bound in chains, caught in cords of affliction, ⁹ then he shows them their deeds — their sins of pride and arrogance. ¹⁰ He opens their ears to correction and commands them to turn from evil.

¹¹ If they obey and serve him, they live out their days in prosperity, their years in contentment. ¹² But if they refuse to listen, they die by the sword, they perish in their ignorance. ¹³ The godless in heart harbor resentment; they do not cry out when he binds them. ¹⁴ They die in their youth, their lives snuffed out among the male cult prostitutes. ¹⁵ But God delivers the afflicted through their affliction; he uses their suffering to open their ears.

¹⁶ He would have drawn you, too, out of the jaws of distress into a spacious place — a place of ease, where your table would overflow with rich food. ¹⁷ But you are filled with the sentence of the wicked; judgment and justice grip you. ¹⁸ Beware that anger does not lead you astray, and do not let a great ransom tempt you to act wrongly. ¹⁹ Will your wealth or all your powerful resources keep you from distress? ²⁰ Do not long for the night, when people vanish from their place.

²¹ Be careful — do not turn to iniquity, for you seem to have chosen this path over your affliction. ²² See how God is exalted in his power; what teacher is there like him? ²³ Who has appointed him his way? Who can say to him, 'You have done wrong'? ²⁴ Remember to extol his work, which people have sung about. ²⁵ All humanity has seen it; mortals gaze at it from afar.

²⁶ How great is God — beyond our knowing; the number of his years is past searching out! ²⁷ He draws up the water droplets; they distill as rain into the streams ²⁸ that the clouds pour down, drenching the multitudes of people. ²⁹ Who can understand how he spreads the clouds or how the thunder rolls from his dwelling? ³⁰ See how he scatters his lightning around him, bathing the depths of the sea in light.

³¹ By these things he governs the peoples; he provides food in abundance. ³² He fills his hands with lightning and commands it to strike its mark. ³³ His thunder announces the coming storm; even the cattle sense its approach.
